facts.statement: Fossils of Erectopus have been found in the Lower Cretaceous La Penthiève Beds Formation of France and possibly the Cernavodă Formation of Romania.
facts.quote: from the Lower Cretaceous La Penthiève Beds Formation of France and also possibly the Cernavodă Formation of southern Romania

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in the early 1870s in phosphate-bearing beds at Louppy-le-Château in eastern France.
facts.quote: The holotype, specimen MNHN 2001-4, was discovered during the early 1870s in the phosphate-bearing beds of La Penthiève (Mammilatum Zone; lower Albian) at Louppy-le-Château in eastern France

facts.statement: Charles Barrois first described the initial fossils, consisting of two teeth and a vertebra, in 1875.
facts.quote: The first, two teeth and a vertebra, were first described by Charles Barrois in 1875

facts.statement: Henri-Émile Sauvage established the species Megalosaurus superbus in 1882 based on these remains.
facts.quote: In 1882 Henri-Émile Sauvage made them the basis for a new taxon, Megalosaurus superbus

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene created the genus Erectopus and named the species Erectopus superbus in 1923.
facts.quote: In 1923, the material was redescribed by Friedrich von Huene, who argued that it could not be included within the genus Megalosaurus and created for the Pierson theropod a separate genus, naming the species Erectopus superbus

facts.statement: In 1932, von Huene proposed a second species, Erectopus sauvagei, believing the original Barrois fossils belonged to a different species.
facts.quote: In 1932 von Huene concluded that the original fossils described by Barrois were not necessarily of the same species as the later finds

facts.statement: The recovered maxilla serves as the lectotype, while the casts of the original Pierson specimen serve as the plastotype.
facts.quote: The recovered maxilla has been designated a lectotype, and the casts of Pierson's specimen has become the plastotype for the taxon

facts.statement: Ronan Allain estimated the weight of Erectopus superbus at 200 kg.
facts.quote: Allain estimated the weight at 200 kg

facts.statement: A 2016 study estimated Erectopus superbus to be 5 meters long and weigh 315 kg.
facts.quote: In 2016 it was estimated to be 5 meters (16 ft) in length and 315 kg (694 lbs) in weight

facts.statement: Allain (2005) classified Erectopus superbus within the Allosauroidea, a group equivalent to Carnosauria.
facts.quote: Allain (2005) placed Erectopus superbus within the Allosauroidea (a concept equivalent to Carnosauria, a term some researchers prefer)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Erectopus as Metriacanthosauridae.
Erectopus lived during the Barremian to Cenomanian stages, between 125.77 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Cenomanian (125.77 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The name Erectopus translates to "upright foot".
